title: A1-18 · The perfect; the denial withمَا‎

blocks.text: A1-18 · The perfect; the denial with ⁧مَا⁩
Lesson overview

⁧دَرَسْتُ⁩ I have studied it. ⁧ذَهَبَ⁩ It's gone. ⁧قَالَ الوَزِيرُ⁩ The Minister said: "" With the perfect ( ⁧المَاضِي⁩ al-māḍī ) short stories concluded actions: what you did yesterday, the weekend, last year. It is also the time of the news: almost every news begins with a verb to the perfect. In this unity learn conjugation, negation with ⁧مَا⁩ and the vocabulary to tell. Two weeks.

rows: 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 41–42 of the calendar)

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Anki deck A1 (tag A1-18), voice synthesis script, tutor session in the second week
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. to combine the perfect with the singular and the persons (s) and (s) of their own;
2. recognize all other people of the perfect;
3. use the most frequent irregular perfects ( ⁧قَالَ⁩ , ⁧زَارَ⁩ , ⁧نَامَ⁩ , ⁧رَأَى⁩ ...) at least the third person and the first person;
4. deny the past with ⁧مَا⁩ and recognize denial with ⁧لَمْ⁩ ;
5. tell your day yesterday and your weekend in 70 words;
6. To understand a slow story to the past and a short story.
Two-week plan.

blocks.text: 1. Dialogue 1 · What did you do yesterday?
Monday morning, in the office.

rows: Karīm: ṣabāḥu l-ḫayri yā Lūkā. māḏā faʿalta ams?
KarīmGood morning, Luca. What did you do yesterday?
Lūkā: ḏahabtu ilā bayti uḫtī, wa-akalnā l- ġadāʾa maʿan.
Luca: I went to my sister's house and we had lunch together.
Lūkā: raǧaʿtu ilā Mīlānū wa-darastu l- ʿarabiyya. katabtu t-tamārīna wa-samiʿtu l-ḥiwārāt. wa-anta?
Luca: I went back to Milan and studied Arabic. I wrote the exercises and listened to the dialogues. What about you?
! ⁧أَنَا مَا خَرَجْتُ مِنَ البَيْتِ⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ ⁧قَرَأْتُ كِتَابًا وَشَاهَدْتُ فِيلْمًا⁩ . ⁧مَغْرِبِيًّا⁩
Karīm: anā mā ḫaraǧtu mina l-bayt! qaraʾtu kitāban wa-šāhadtu fīlman maġribiyyan.
Karīm: I didn't leave the house! I read a book and saw a Moroccan movie.

blocks.text: ⁧الفِيلْمُ بِالدَّارِجَةِ، وَأَنَا⁩ ! ⁧طَبْعًا⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ Karīm: ṭabʿan! al-fīlmu bi-d-dāriǧa, wa- Karīm: Sure! The movie is in Darija, and I am! ⁧مَغْرِبِيٌّ⁩ anā maġribī! Moroccan!

What to notice. All forms with -you are -Io- ( ⁧ذَهَبْتُ⁩ , ⁧رَجَعْتُ⁩ , ⁧دَرَسْتُ⁩ ); con -ta sono ⁧فَعَلْتَ⁩ , ⁧فَهِمْتَ⁩ ); with -nā "Noi" ( ⁧أَكَلْنَا⁩ ). ⁧مَا خَرَجْتُ⁩ I have not gone out of the past: denial of the past. ⁧الدَّارِجَة⁩ is the name of Arabic spoken in Morocco: the film is in dialect, and that's why Luca asks the question.
2. The perfect: singular shapes
The perfect form with suffixes added to a base (daras-, kataba-): no prefixes.
She ⁧ـَتْ⁩ -at ⁧دَرَسَتْ⁩ darasat

Me, you, you - just the final vowel. ⁧دَرَسْتُ⁩ / ⁧دَرَسْتَ⁩ / ⁧دَرَسْتِ⁩ equals without vowels ( ⁧درست⁩ ). In non-vocational texts, it decides the context; Reading aloud, he pronounces the final vowel well: in pause these suffixes do not fall. The form "lui" is the form of the dictionary (A1-13): ⁧دَرَسَ⁩ , ⁧كَتَبَ⁩ . In pause you read daras, katab. You are in front of the article: ⁧دَرَسَتِ الطَّالِبَةُ⁩ darasates ṭ-ṭāliba , with support.
3. The Voice of the Perfect
The basis of the perfect has the shape CaCaC-, CaCiC- or, rarely, CaCuC-. You learn it with the verb: you find it in the vocabulary of A1-13.
⁧عَرَفَ⁩ a ⁧عَرَفْتُيَعْرِفُ⁩ know, know
A useful rule. If the perfect one has an i ( ⁧عَمِلَ⁩ , ⁧شَرِبَ⁩ , ⁧فَهِمَ⁩ ), the imperfect has almost always a ( ⁧يَعْمَلُ⁩ , ⁧يَشْرَبُ⁩ , ⁧يَفْهَمُ⁩ ). The opposite is not true.

The alif muta of -ū. ⁧دَرَسُوا⁩ is written with a final alif that is not pronounced ( darasū ): is the separation You don't write in front of a suffix: ⁧دَرَسُوهُ⁩ They studied it. The most frequent are ...-nā) and their (-ū): Use them actively. The others recognize them. The agreement with the subject follows the rules of A1-14: verb before subject to singular ( ⁧ذَهَبَ الطُّلَّابُ⁩ • students have gone to school, ⁧قَالَ الوُزَرَاءُ⁩ The ministers said, after the plural subject ( ⁧الطُّلَّابُ ذَهَبُوا⁩ ).
5. Perfect frequent irregulars
Some verbs have a changing base. Learn them as words: they are among the most used.
⁧أَحْبَبْتُأَحَبَّتْأَحَبَّ⁩ ⁧يُحِبُّأَحَبُّوا⁩ love

Because they change. In ⁧قَالَ⁩ , ⁧زَارَ⁩ , ⁧نَامَ⁩ , ⁧كَانَ⁩ the second consonant of the root is ⁧و⁩ or ⁧ي⁩ ( ⁧ق و ل⁩ , ⁧ز و ر⁩ , ⁧ن و م⁩ , ⁧ك و ن⁩ ): becomes ā long to 3in person and disappears, shortening the vowel, in front of the suffixes in consonant (qultu , zurtu , nimtu , kuntu). It's the family of verbs "concavi": you will study it thoroughly in A2. ⁧كَانَ⁩ It was, it was. Enough for now in phrases like ⁧كَانَ الدَّرْسُ صَعْبًا⁩ The lesson was difficult and ⁧كُنْتُ فِي رُومَا⁩ I was in Rome. How ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ , puts the predicate to the accusative (A1-19).
6. The denial of the past: ⁧مَا⁩
. ⁧أَكَلْنَا⁩ . ⁧مَا أَكَلْنَا⁩ We didn't eat.

⁧مَا⁩ in front of the perfect is a correct denial of the standard Arabic, frequent in the educated speech and in many texts. To be recognized: . ⁧لَمْ⁩ In the prose journalistic and administrative past is more often denied with ⁧لَمْ⁩ + imperfect apocopate (without the final -u): ⁧لَمْ أَذْهَبْ⁩ I didn't go, ⁧لَمْ يَقُلْ⁩ • did not say: • The meaning is the same; form you will study it in A2. When you read ⁧لَمْ⁩ , think of the negative past. Do not confuse ⁧مَا⁩ denial (before a verb to the perfect) with ⁧مَا⁩ What? (in front of a name, A1-05): ⁧مَا فَهِمْتُ⁩ I don't understand. ⁧مَا هٰذَا؟⁩ What is it?
7. Telling: expressions of time

⁧أَمْسِ⁩ Yesterday. ⁧البَارِحَةَ⁩ Last night, yesterday. ⁧الأُسْبُوعَ المَاضِيَ⁩ Last week, it's gonna be okay. ⁧السَّنَةَ المَاضِيَةَ⁩ Last year. ⁧قَبْلَ أُسْبُوعٍ⁩ 1 week ago ⁧قَبْلَ سَنَتَيْنِ⁩ 2 years ago. ⁧مُنْذُ⁩ ( ⁧مُنْذُ سَنَةٍ⁩ (One year) · ⁧أَوَّلًا⁩ … ⁧ثُمَّ⁩ … ⁧بَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ⁩ … ⁧فِي النِّهَايَةِ⁩ First... Then... After... at the end of the day. ⁧قَبْلَ⁩ and ⁧مُنْذُ⁩ . ⁧قَبْلَ⁩ + time = ⁧زُرْتُ القَاهِرَةَ قَبْلَ سَنَتَيْنِ⁩ I visited Cairo two years ago. ⁧مُنْذُ⁩ + time with imperfection = ⁧أَسْكُنُ فِي مِيلَانُو مُنْذُ سَنَةٍ⁩ I have lived in Milan for one year.

Monday night, at the class.

Salmā: Nice! And did you study (you two)?
Yūsuf: No... we didn't study much.
⁧بَقِيتُ فِي⁩ . ⁧أَنَا مَا سَافَرْتُ⁩ : ⁧مَارْيَا⁩ . ⁧البَيْتِ وَكَتَبْتُ تَقْرِيرًا لِلشَّرِكَةِ⁩
Māryā: anā mā sāfartu. baqītu fī l- bayti wa-katabtu taqrīran li-š-šarika.
I didn't leave. I stayed home and wrote a report for the company.
⁧هِيَ عَمِلَتْ يَوْمَ السَّبْتِ،⁩ : ⁧مَارْيَا⁩ ! ⁧وَيَوْمَ الأَحَدِ نَامَتْ حَتَّى الظُّهْرِ⁩

blocks.text: What to notice. ⁧فَعَلْتُمْ⁩ You have done this (you), ⁧دَرَسْتُمَا⁩ You have studied (you two), ⁧زُرْنَا⁩ We have visited the site (perfect irregular of ⁧زَارَ⁩ ). ⁧بَقِيتُ⁩ I have remained is another irregular verb (roots ⁧ب ق ي⁩ ): Learn it as a block. ⁧حَتَّى⁩ • up to and including.
9. The Perfect in the News

rows: The Foreign Minister arrived yesterday in Cairo.
The Prime Minister met with the Italian Ambassador.
The president visited the city of Basra.

blocks.text: The typical scheme: verb to perfect (3a singular person) + subject + complements + time. The first verb tells you what happened; the subject immediately after, who did. In B1 Read authentic news with this structure. ⁧قَالَ⁩ … ⁧إِنَّ⁩ • said that: the complete construction is in A2.
10. Pronunciation

- You, -ta, -ti. Three different suffixes only in vowel: darastu, darast, darasti. Exercise with the B script until you distinguish them at first listening. The sukūn before the suffix. : ⁧دَرَسْتُ⁩ The s has no voice, daras-tu. Don't say darasatu. -ū and -ā Finals. darasū (they) darasā (they two): ū and ā long; the after-life wāw You don't read. ⁧قُلْتُ⁩ , ⁧زُرْتُ⁩ , ⁧نِمْتُ⁩ . Short voice: qultu , zurtu , nimtu . All 3long person: qāla , zāra , nāma .
11. New lexicon

rows: I don't understand ( ⁧مَا⁩ denies the perfect)

⁧الدَّارِجَة⁩ ad-dāriǧa Arab spoken of the Maghreb ⁧د ر ج⁩ name f.

Notes of use. ⁧شَاهَدَ⁩ it is used for films, television, games; ⁧رَأَى⁩ is the generic view. ⁧كَلِمَة⁩ means "word" and also "discourse," intervention ( ⁧كَلِمَةُ الوَزِيرِ⁩ The Minister's intervention is therefore in order. For the taxi is also said. ⁧تَاكْسِي الدَّارِجَة⁩ ( o ⁧الدَّارِجَة المَغْرِبِيَّة⁩ ) is the Moroccan dialect; Similar terms are used in Algeria and Tunisia.
